creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A sidebar row reads `nook · claude` - a directory and a harness
(`roster.rs::pane_label`). At fifteen panes that is fifteen rows saying
almost the same thing, and the founding promise is that you can tell
sessions apart at a glance.

Ghostty names its tabs after whatever the program in them is doing.
That is not Ghostty being clever: Claude Code sets the terminal title
with OSC 2 and the terminal displays it. **herdr already tracks it.**
Read off a live pane today:

    agent                    'claude'
    agent_status             'idle'
    terminal_title           '✳ nook-first-working-build'
    terminal_title_stripped  'nook-first-working-build'

Stripped of the status glyph for us, per pane, in `pane.get` and
`pane.list`. Nothing upstream is needed - `RosterPane` needs the field
and the sidebar needs to draw it.

**The daemon is the only possible source, which settles where this
lives.** libghostty hands the app a title for a surface it is painting,
but the sidebar exists to show panes *no region is showing*, and those
have no surface. So a renderer-sourced title would be blank on exactly
the rows this feature is for.

Worth deciding rather than defaulting:

- **A second line, and when to draw one.** Two lines times fifteen panes
  is roughly double the height of a list whose value is being glanceable.
  Lean: draw the second line only when there is a title worth showing, so
  plain shells stay one line and agents get the room. That is
  self-limiting in the right direction.
- **What "worth showing" means, which is not "present".** oh-my-zsh sets
  a title by default, usually the directory or the running command - the
  two things the row already says. So the rule is not "show it when it
  exists" but "show it when it says something the first line does not",
  and that comparison is a decision the core should make once rather than
  the shell making it per row.
- **Wrapping or truncating.** Wrapping a long title in a 200pt list makes
  the row height a function of what the agent is doing, so the list jumps
  under the reader while an agent works. Lean: one line, tail-truncated,
  full text on hover. Stability beats completeness in a list you are
  meant to scan.
- **Whether the tab caption takes it too**, which is what the screenshot
  actually shows. A tab holding one agent has an obvious name available.
  herdr labels tabs by workspace and number, so this would be Muster
  overriding a daemon label - decidable, but a different decision from
  the pane row and worth making separately.

**Measure before building**: how often does the title change? Claude
rewrites it as it works, and a roster republished on every change is a
cost that lands at frequency times cardinality, which is the budget this
project holds itself to. Fifteen agents each rewriting a title is the
case to measure, and it may argue for coalescing title changes rather
than treating them like any other roster event.

**Do not log it.** A title is derived from what somebody typed to their
agent. "Terminals carry secrets, so what you typed is never in the run
log unless you ask for it" applies to this as much as to keystrokes -
the field should be carried and drawn, and named but not quoted in any
diagnostic.
title: 🏷️ Say what each agent is working on, not just where it lives
